主要内容: On August 1, 2014, the Federal Reserve Board (FRB) released FEDS Notes outlining the Enhanced Financial Accounts (EFAs) project. This initiative aims to significantly improve the Financial Accounts of the United States by providing more detailed and timely data on financial intermediation. The EFAs project includes larger-scale changes such as higher-frequency information and more-disaggregated data, even if these data are not fully integrated into the existing structure. The Financial Accounts, previously known as the Flow of Funds Accounts, are U.S. national accounts published quarterly by the FRB. They provide macro-financial flows and balance sheets for major sectors like households, financial institutions, and governments. The project also aims to enhance the usability of the Financial Accounts by improving data reporting and providing additional documentation. The EFAs project is part of the FRB's ongoing effort to improve financial accounting practices and better understand economic relationships. The FRB has outlined plans to significantly enhance the Financial Accounts to provide more detailed information on financial instruments and risk exposures. The Enhanced Financial Accounts (EFA) Project aims to improve the detail, dimensionality, and scope of the Financial Accounts by offering data at higher frequencies, more disaggregated levels, and for both market and book values. The project includes expanding information on financial derivatives, which are crucial for transferring market, credit, interest-rate, and exchange-rate risks. The enhancements will be integrated into the core of the Financial Accounts for some sectors, while others will be presented as supplementary data. The FRB is also exploring ways to improve data dissemination and communication about the Financial Accounts, including the use of new tools and analysis. These changes are intended to provide analysts and researchers with more detailed insights into the financial system.
